subject: literature
passage: Dear Cousin, You will forgive the brevity of this letter, for my engagements in Town leave me scarcely an hour to myself. I dine abroad almost every evening, and have been twice to the theater, where the company was so brilliant that I quite forgot the play. Pray do not imagine that I miss the country; I assure you I think of it very seldom. I should be obliged, however, if you would tell me whether the old pear tree by the mill has borne this year, and whether my mare is properly exercised, and whether the Marsh family still sit in the third pew, and whether you yourself walk to the brook on Sunday afternoons as we used to do. Your affectionate cousin, Edmund
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To suggest that the writer has been too busy in Town to remember his former life very clearly
choices.B: To reveal, through the writer's own words, a longing for home that undercuts his denials
choices.C: To describe the social pleasures that a fashionable young man could enjoy while living in Town
choices.D: To show that the writer resents his cousin for having chosen to remain behind in the country

explanation.why: Edmund insists he is too busy to write at length and that he thinks of the country "very seldom." Then, with "however," he asks a long, loving string of questions about the pear tree, his mare, the neighbors' pew, and Sunday walks "as we used to do." His detailed questions betray the homesickness he denies, which is the point of the letter.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Edmund remembers small details of home vividly, from the pear tree to the third pew, so the letter shows the reverse.
explanation.B: Correct. The many affectionate questions about home contradict Edmund's claim that he seldom thinks of the country.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The dinners and theater appear only in the opening lines, which the rest of the letter undercuts.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Edmund signs himself "affectionate" and fondly recalls walks with his cousin; nothing suggests resentment.
